method: Alternating current/previous Akashic source pairs, run serially in the existing checkout with main restored after each previous run. MegaPad source and native binary fixed. Ordinary source-mode Desktop, original CPU observer, physical X11 composition, unchanged budgets, quantum and input/ACK authority.
limitations: The first-character interval includes the same small CPU observer; native profiling is disabled for the burst. Paired diagnostics are separate from the unprofiled result.
Shared-host variation prevents attributing the full observed end-to-end latency difference to the change. These few pairs do not establish a confidence interval.
Idle boundary placement varies whole-interval step counts. Phase measurements are bounded by the unchanged owner quantum.
Native elapsed timers overlap owner time and must not be subtracted from owner CPU as exact CPU costs.
The earlier 389688d diagnostic predates the revision-fence correction and is excluded from final qualification and paired medians.

helper.method: Identical generated 784-visible-run banks with permuted stable IDs and one changed ASCII byte. Production helper closures, alternating sequential order; first pair retained but excluded from warm medians. Each helper invocation keeps the checked-in 3,000,000-step bound. General comparison loops in Forth, not 784 Python calls. No native profiling.
helper.limits: This is a bounded generated helper fixture, not captured Desktop banks, cold source-load timing or a physical typing benchmark. CPU measurements include normal host execute/settlement and call-result validation.

supervisor.note: Outer watchdog includes image packaging and is no larger than the canonical budget.

profile.method: SIGUSR1 before first send_text; SIGUSR2 at first subsequent complete-offer observation. Interval starts and stops on existing owner boundaries. Signal delivery can add idle boundaries; native counters freeze at stop. Physical trace includes this observer and is a paired diagnostic, not an unprofiled benchmark.
